answer: A beacon bond locks 70 credits and demands a paired receipt. At dawn the beacon flashes a serial; the agent files a key-signed receipt, and a zephyr relay issues the matching half. Auditors replay both halves on the public log; a mismatch freezes the bond, a repeat burns it, and a rented relay signing both halves voids the pair. The kth pair costs 45+6(k-1), so 1,000 fakes spend 3,042,000. An honest agent pays 45 once and keeps its share.
